history.summary: A large 980 sqft 2BR at $1,602 psf (~2% under the $1,635 median) in a BCA Construction-Excellence-awarded, 1,145-unit Hougang development — meaning best-in-batch resale liquidity (292 URA txns) and proven build quality. 7.5% resale CAGR is well-supported. The 1.06km MRT walk is the one real drawback, but the liquidity + quality combination makes it a Buy.
history.rating_rationale: The Minton's scale is its edge: 1,145 units and 292 URA transactions give the deepest resale liquidity in this batch — you can exit. It won BCA Construction Excellence (Merit) and LIAS Gold awards, so build/landscaping quality is documented rather than guessed, and reviews describe it as quiet and uncrowded despite the size. 7.5% resale CAGR is high-confidence on 292 txns, and a 980 sqft 2BR at $1,602 psf is roughly at median (fair entry). Drawbacks: 1.06km to Serangoon MRT (no near-station premium) and it is the one off-frontier listing here (slightly below the efficient set). Liquidity + quality outweigh the walk.

agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: 7.5% resale CAGR on a deep 292-txn base is among the most trustworthy here; expect continued solid mid-single-digit appreciation underpinned by liquidity and quality.

history.summary: A 1,145-unit Hougang mega-development with deep 292-txn liquidity and 7.5%/yr URA resale appreciation, but this specific 3BR is priced at PSF 1873 — a steep ~14% PREMIUM over the project's URA median of 1635 — at a $2.5M quantum that thins the buyer pool. Recurring build-quality complaints (water seepage, low-grade finishes) and a 1km+ MRT walk make this overpriced unit an Avoid.
history.rating_rationale: The project fundamentals are fine (292 txns = very liquid, 7.5%/yr resale CAGR, large facilities), but you are not buying the project at median — you are buying one unit at PSF 1873 vs a URA median of 1635, a ~14% premium. At a $2.5M quantum that premium is hard to recover on exit, and the buyer pool above $2.4M is materially shallower. Reviews repeatedly cite poor interior finishing, ceiling water seepage and piping/water-supply disruptions, which depress resale appeal. The 1.06km walk to Serangoon MRT is a further drag. Good development, bad price.
